paper.title: AutoHarness: improving LLM agents by automatically synthesizing a code harness
paper.central_claim: Automatically synthesized executable harnesses prevent illegal actions and improve frozen-model gameplay; an extreme code-policy variant removes inference-time LLM calls.

provenance.notes: sonnet slot configured as gpt-6.1-sol per dispatch; independently verifiable model receipt/session ID unavailable, no probe.

sections_read: Appendix A all145-game table and observation examples

evidence.quote: we employ a tree search guided by Thompson sampling
evidence.support_explanation: Search over persistent executable harnesses; borrowed search lineage, not a new optimizer proof.

evidence.quote:
If
is_legal_action()
returns
True
but the action is invalid, we refine both functions
evidence.support_explanation: Conditional component-level repair uses environment legality feedback.

evidence.quote: if invalid, repeats the process with a new prompt that includes an “illegal action” warning message
evidence.support_explanation: Verifier intervention includes extra inference attempts; matched retry control required.

evidence.quote:
At most 5 failed steps are sampled and fed to the
Critic
evidence.support_explanation: Ten parallel environments, at most1000 steps; source/errors inform code refinement.

evidence.quote: Training ends when the heuristic value (i.e. the legal action success rate) reaches 1.0, or we time out.
evidence.support_explanation: Search stopping criterion uses training legality, not formal proof.

evidence.quote: On average, training ends after 14.5 tree search iterations, while 19/32 games end in less than 10 iterations.
evidence.support_explanation: Partial search accounting for32-game scope; not average over all145.

evidence.quote: novel test rollouts (of length 1000, across 10 random random seeds per game)
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit novel-seed test rollouts; not unseen games or repeated synthesis seeds.

evidence.quote: We achieved 100% legal action success rate for all the games
evidence.support_explanation: Observed zero invalid test actions, not universal validity certification.

evidence.quote: For 1P games, we run 20 matches and use the reward as the evaluation metric.
evidence.support_explanation: Outcome metric and denominator specified; no textual intervals or significance.

evidence.quote: For 2P games, we run 40 matches with random seeds, split evenly between our method being the first or second player

evidence.support_explanation: Small Flash plus harness outperforms Pro in reported aggregate matchup; not all games.

evidence.quote: On average, we achieve 0.745 reward, in comparison to 0.707 (Gemini-2.5-Pro) and 0.673 (Gemini-2.5-Flash).
evidence.support_explanation: Reported same-model package benefit and stronger-model comparison.

evidence.quote: On average, training takes 89.4 iterations and achieves a heuristic value of 0.939.
evidence.support_explanation: Full code-policy variant has separate search budget and objective.

evidence.quote: our approach achieves the highest average reward (0.870)
evidence.support_explanation: Code-policy result is domain-program performance, not edited-improver evidence.

evidence.quote: which are repeated 10 and 5 times, for cost reasons.
evidence.support_explanation: GPT5.2/High use fewer evaluation repetitions, not search-run variance.

evidence.quote: the GPT-5.2 and GPT-5.2-High experiments cost approximately $640.
evidence.support_explanation: Comparator evaluation spending only; missing complete synthesis/retry cost and break-even.

evidence.quote: Currently we generate a separate harness for each environment (game).
evidence.support_explanation: No measured cross-game retained library; recursive distillation/library explicitly future work.

evidence.quote: removing any form of “Available Moves” hints in the observation string
evidence.support_explanation: Rules are not supplied as explicit action lists in selected modified observations.

evidence.quote: This leaves us with 145 games, including well-known games
evidence.support_explanation: Coverage includes parameterized variants; end-to-end comparison restricted to32.

signatures.object: Executable propose_action/is_legal_action harness around frozen game-playing LLM
signatures.information: Harness source plus environment legality failures, sampled steps and error messages
signatures.operation: Thompson tree search selects program parents; critic consolidates failures; LLM refines appropriate functions
signatures.output: Selected executable verifier reused for later game rollouts
signatures.conditions: Reliable environment legality feedback and parseable observation/action interface
signatures.feedback: Actual environment invalid-action/code failures; reward for separate policy variant
signatures.selection_rule: Average legal-action accuracy; stop at1.0 or timeout; tree-search history retains candidates
signatures.selection_data: Ten parallel training environments with at most1000steps; separate novel-seed test rollouts reported
signatures.persistence: Generated Python harness code retained after search
signatures.later_use: Fixed verifier filters future LLM proposals and triggers re-prompt; separate code-policy variant executes without LLM
signatures.claimed_effect: Fewer invalid moves and better game outcomes without updating model weights
signatures.failure_boundary: Per-game synthesis; learned checker has no universal soundness proof; extra retry compute not matched

gap.author_gap: LLMs lose games through illegal actions; manually engineering control harnesses is laborious.
gap.checked_gap: Environment-checked generated verifier addresses demonstrated legality failure, but optimizer novelty and superiority over simpler repair/search remain unisolated.

G.reason: Concrete illegal-move/human-authoring gap, but known program-search lineage and closest original priority unresolved.

M.reason: Generated verifier directly addresses control failures and is retained for later rollouts; per-game specialization bounds generality.

X.reason: Interfaces, mutation/fitness, error-conditioned function repair, prompts, stopping and code examples specified; complete generated implementations/selection internals not fully supplied.

E.measurement.reason: Actual environment legality/reward and balanced game outcomes are meaningful; learned-checker false rejection and universal-soundness claim not audited.

E.causality.reason: Same Flash and common prompt with/without harness tests joint effect; extra verifier retries and no simpler-search/critic-off controls prevent clean mechanism attribution.

E.holdout.reason: Novel-seed rollouts explicitly separate training from reporting; no frozen unseen-game/task holdout, exact seed partition and promotion isolation audit absent.

E.statistics.reason: Test seed/match counts and negative per-game outcomes reported; no uncertainty intervals/significance or independent synthesis-run variance. Repeated gameplay means do not constitute uncertainty estimates.

E.cost.reason: Search iterations and comparator640-dollar evaluation cost are partial accounting; full proposer tokens, retries, runtime and amortized break-even absent.
